title: theOS owns avenSANDBOX
note: theOS takes avenSANDBOX whole (d-0a23): its name, its image with every tool, its image workflow and its cloud setup. avenDB's release, peer image and deploy stay parked; the release is aip-59ad.

questions.q: Move avenSANDBOX into theOS (theOS owns it and its release from then on), or copy it and leave avenDB's release where it is? And who releases the box afterwards?
options: Copy it into theOS; avenDB keeps releasing until theOS's copy passes its gates (recommended: no release path changes before Gate A)
Move it: theOS owns it and its release now

questions.q: Gate A for aip-6fb1, after its spec review: are its claims, assumptions, checkpoint plan, outcome and mockup what must be true?

Checkpoint 2's Review gate ran three rounds without a clean one (c2-review: 3, 2 and 1 Major; every finding answered). Round 3's only Major (the smoke could not fail on a wrong platform) is fixed, tried here, and proven by the image workflow's run on the fixed commit (in the events). By the rule, patching stopped: pass the gate with that run as proof, run one more round, or send checkpoint 2 back to Understand?
options: Pass it: the fix is proven by its run (recommended: the open finding was mechanical and a machine now checks it)

questions.q: avenCEO changes proposed by aip-6fb1's run (one avenCEO intent each, measured before kept). Which do you want as intents?
options: 1. A check is a file: every claim's check names a script in theOS that a machine runs; an event says verified only with that script's run (l-006d, l-9f44). Measured by: checkpoint review findings of kind 'missing check' (7 of 15 in c2, 2 of 4 Blocker/Major in c3).
2. Events stamped by a machine: a small append script writes at, by and the commit; nobody types a time (l-d7ef). Measured by: lead time per step readable to the minute; errata on times.
3. Every finding carries a kind, in the review type and both checker prompts (l-f324). Measured by: the share of findings with a kind (today 0 of 55 in spec review).

4. Spec review stops at one round when you are reachable: the zoom-out lens checks deletions against the source first, and three rounds turn into one round plus your answer (l-18a8). Measured by: spec rounds and your corrections per intent (aip-6fb1: 3 rounds, 6 agents, 55 findings, 1 correction).

who: Samuel Andert, who wants one authority for what ships, and runs the box on a Mac.
avenMAIA, whose sessions start from the environment avenSANDBOX warms, and whose checks run in the box.
problem.experience: avenSANDBOX gives every scenario the same clean box: a cloud session, a GitHub runner, a Mac with OrbStack. But its image is defined and built from avenDB's files, its workflow is parked, and nothing in theOS starts it, so theOS's checks have no box of their own.

items.text: avensandbox.yml released avenOS, avenSANDBOX and avenPEER from production, each under a dated version; the last release is #1750 (avenOS 26.10.31v6, avenPEER 26.10.31v5, avenSANDBOX 26.10.31v2).
avensandbox-image.yml and avenpeer-image.yml built their images from aven/DB2's Cargo workspace.
avendeploy.yml deployed the avenCEO Peer and avenOS at aven.maia.city, by hand.
aven/DB2/sandbox/box/Dockerfile compiles avenDB's third-party crates; cloud-setup.sh runs avenDB's bun run up, four avenDB peers, once before the snapshot.
This session: dockerd is not running; /var/log/dockerd.log last written 29 Oct; /var/lib/docker holds 24 GB; bun, node and Chromium (/opt/pw-browsers) come with the base image.
The environment's setup script looks only for aven/DB2/sandbox/box/cloud-setup.sh, and exits 0 when it is not there (aven/DB2/SANDBOX.md, "Samuel's part").

problem.baseline: Before the park: four workflows, all avenDB's. theOS has no box, no workflow and no release of its own.
whys: theOS's checks have no clean box of their own. Why? avenSANDBOX's image is defined, tagged and built from avenDB's files, and its workflow is parked with avenDB's.
Why? It was built for avenDB (29 to 31 Oct) before theOS became the standalone project (d-9351).
Root cause: avenSANDBOX belongs to a legacy project.
truths: GitHub runs the workflow files of the branch an event happens on; a file moved out of .github/workflows/ on that branch never runs there.
A deployed server keeps serving what it was last given until something deploys again.
An image already published to a registry stays pullable when its workflow stops.
A workflow file must live in .github/workflows/; what it runs can live in theOS/.
assumptions: avenSANDBOX keeps every tool (d-0a23): Playwright 1.64.1 with its Chromium, Rust stable with wasm32 and wasm-bindgen, the nightly with cargo-fuzz, bun, elan with Lean, versitygw, clang and llvm.
Only avenDB's own part stays behind: the step that compiles avenDB's third-party crates. avenDB's bun run up stops working when the box moves; avenDB is parked.
The image keeps its name, ghcr.io/myavenceo/aven/sandbox, and stays public; the environment already allows ghcr.io and pkg-containers.githubusercontent.com.
The image is the only source of the browser: theOS's lockfile pins its Playwright (1.64.1).
The work reaches main through the goal pull request you ask for after Gate B; the environment's snapshot clones main.
Pasting the environment's script and the Mac run are yours, at Gate B.
problem.risk: Can be undone: the move by git mv back (tried in a scratch checkout); the environment's script by pasting the previous one, kept in theOS/sandbox/; the image's old tags stay pullable. The environment's script is shared by every session in it. production is frozen by its ruleset; it moves with the release (aip-59ad). The environment's undo restores the previous script, which still never fails a session but has no time limit, and its avenDB warm-up (bun run up) fails since the box moved.

reuse.use: Learned from: production takes changes from main only; one release per changed package, under the date (26.10.29, 26.10.29v2, ...); a push that changes nothing releases nothing.
Learned from: the image is tagged by the hash of the files its build reads, so every checkout runs exactly its own box; built per architecture, then joined.

reuse.what: aven/DB2/sandbox/box/cloud-setup.sh and the environment's setup script
reuse.use: Learned from: warm the box once, before the disk is snapshotted; never fail a session.
Learned from: run by hand in the environment production; health checks after the deploy; nothing secret printed, the repository is public.

claims.fails: The check passes in one scenario and fails in another.

outcome.promise: theOS's check command runs in one avenSANDBOX image built from theOS/, with the same result on the same commit in every scenario; nothing of avenDB is read to build, start or warm it.

The process, as aip-6fb1's measure says (the outcome claim is not measured yet: it needs checkpoint 4 and Gate B). Lead time: asked 08:51, understood 09:12 (21 min); Specify 09:12 to Gate A 09:53 (41 min, 3 spec rounds); Build from 09:54: checkpoint 2 built 10:00, its Review gate 10:02 to 10:16 (3 rounds); checkpoint 3 started 09:58, its gate clean 10:17. Many events share a minute (4 to 6 at 09:12, 09:21, 09:53), so time inside a step is not readable. Sent back: spec 3 rounds, none clean (Gate A by d-9f02's shortcut); checkpoint 2, 3 rounds, none clean; checkpoint 3, 2 rounds, clean on the second. First pass: 0 of 2 checkpoints. Findings: spec rounds 55 (2 Blocker, 29 Major, 24 Nit; 52 fixed, 1 contested, 2 declined; no kind recorded); checkpoint 2, 18 (6 Major, 12 Nit; kinds: missing check 8, bug 3, unclear 4, wrong fact 2, security 1); checkpoint 3, 15 (2 Blocker, 2 Major, 11 Nit; kinds: bug 5, unclear 5, missing check 4, wrong fact 1). Touches: 5 messages from Samuel against the 2 planned (the source; d-a347, an answer to a question asked before the spec; d-0a23, a correction; d-9f02, the go-ahead that was also Gate A; d-2519, how the work runs). Corrections: 1 (d-0a23 reversed revision 3). Escalations: 0 findings needed Samuel; 1 question before the spec (d-a347); 1 now (checkpoint 2's third round). Mechanical share: 4 of 4 claims and the outcome are mechanical. Undos tried: 1 (the move, git mv back, 0.13 s); the environment's undo is Samuel's paste, not tried. Agents spent: 11 fresh checkers (6 spec, 3 for checkpoint 2, 2 for checkpoint 3), no workers: the threads did the work themselves.

What worked: the fresh critic on real diffs found real defects every time, and cheaply (about 1.5 min and one agent a round): a smoke that skipped the Mac's platform, a latest tag ahead of its smoke, run.sh broken on a Mac's bash 3.2, a test with a false pass on a Mac, a test escaping its scratch folder, a smoke that could not fail. None of these were findable by reading the spec, and the spec rounds had not found them. Keeping the critic's prompt and the commit in the review let each round build on the last without re-raising settled findings (one contested with an event the critic had missed).

What cost too much: spec review. Three rounds, six agents and 55 findings before Gate A, then Gate A passed by a shortcut anyway; one round's YAGNI cut (no image) was reversed by Samuel within minutes (d-0a23). The checkpoint rounds then found 33 more findings, 8 Blocker or Major, almost all of a kind no spec reviewer could see (does it run, on which platform, does the test test). The most repeated kind is 'missing check' (12 of 33): claims called verified on one run, a test kept only as an event, a check that could not fail.

What to change (proposed to Samuel as a question, not made): a check is a file a machine runs, and 'verified' needs its run; events stamped by a machine; a kind on every finding; one spec round when Samuel is reachable, with deletions checked against the source first. And one thing to keep: the three-round stop held (checkpoint 2 stopped at round 3 with one mechanical Major, now a question) without blocking checkpoint 3.
